transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes — clean the pump filter first, as fluff can collect there and restrict the water used to condense moisture during drying. A hot or slightly scorched smell can also be fluff overheating where airflow is restricted. 1. If the smell is strongly burning, stop using the drying function, switch off and unplug the machine, and let it cool.
2. With it unplugged, place towels and a shallow tray at the lower front filter flap. Unscrew the pump filter slowly, drain any water, remove fluff/debris, then refit it securely. This is the main owner-cleanable item on many washer-dryers.
3. Check the cold-water tap is fully on and the inlet and drain hoses behind the machine are not kinked or crushed. Washer-dryers commonly need cold water while drying to remove moisture.
4. Dry only a smaller, well-spun load: a washer-dryer’s drying capacity is much lower than its wash capacity. A full wash load often remains damp even without a fault. If it gets properly hot but still dries poorly after those checks, a restriction in the condensing/air path is more likely than a failed heater. If it stays cold on drying, the likely fault is in the drying heater, thermostat or thermal cut-out and it is best left to an engineer. On a drying-only programme, does it become warm/hot but leave the laundry damp, or does it stay cold?

It gets very hot on the dry cycle, the top of the machine is really hot to touch, but the clothes still come out damp. The smell is like burning dust or scorched fabric, and I've kept using it so far. I usually dry a full 8-9kg wash load in one go, straight after washing.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The full 8–9 kg wash load is very likely part of why the clothes remain damp: washer-dryers normally dry substantially less than their wash capacity, often around half. However, it does not make a burning-dust/scorched-fabric smell acceptable. Because it becomes very hot and smells scorched, do not use the drying function again until a qualified appliance engineer has checked it. The most likely cause is fluff or a restriction in the drying/condensing route overheating; a drying heater control or thermal cut-out may also have been affected. The heater itself is clearly producing heat, so this is not simply a “no heat” fault. The pump-filter check is still useful evidence for the engineer, but it does not make the machine safe to resume drying. If it contains a lot of fluff or debris, that supports a restriction in the drying-water/drain route. If it is clear, an internal condensing duct, fan/air path, or overheating control becomes more likely and requires dismantling. For future use only after repair, split washed laundry into loads within the stated dry capacity and use a proper final spin first.

candidates: Fluff restriction in the drying/condensing water path or pump filter (high)
Drying load too large or insufficiently spun (medium)
Drying heater, thermostat or thermal cut-out fault (medium)
